reports.title: MIDERA FOOD PROCESSING REPORTS THIRD QUARTER 2026 RESULTS

guidance.heading: Guidance
section: The Company is updating its full-year 2026 guidance to reflect an increase in the midpoints of its expected ranges for Net sales and Estimated Standalone Adjusted EBITDA1, 2:

(in millions, except percentages) | FY 2025 Actuals | Prior3 | Current | % change vs. FY 20254
Net sales | $853 | $935-965 | $953-973 | ~13%
Change in Organic net sales1, 5 | ~7%
Estimated Standalone Adjusted EBITDA1, 2 | $140 | $160-176 | $168-178 | ~24%
The Company is also providing the following modeling assumptions for full-year 2026:

desk.headline: Net sales up 13% to $228.9m, above estimates, in first quarter as a standalone company; full-year guidance raised

numbers.eps_basis: diluted GAAP; adjusted diluted EPS $0.54 (no prior-year comparison given)

results: In its first quarter since splitting from Middleby in July, net sales rose 13% to $228.9m (11.5% organic), above the $219.9m estimate.
Profit improved sharply: net earnings rose to $20.9m ($0.46 a share) from $14.3m, and adjusted EBITDA jumped 45% to $42.9m, an 18.7% margin.
Growth came from aftermarket parts and service, price rises, and more equipment sales across snack, bakery and protein lines.
Orders rose 13% to $229m, keeping the backlog at a record $446m.
Net debt was $199.8m (1.2x earnings); after quarter-end Midera bought Phoenix Innovations, a poultry-equipment maker with about $25m of annual sales.

guidance.summary: Midera raised its 2026 outlook: net sales of $953–973m (was $935–965m) and estimated standalone adjusted EBITDA of $168–178m (was $160–176m), about 13% and 24% growth at the midpoints.

points: Food makers keep investing in automation, yield and new product formats; snack was the fastest-growing area, helped by equipment delayed from Q2.
Aftermarket parts and service made up 42% of sales and grew about 16%, supported by mid-year parts price increases.
The backlog covers more than 90% of the Q4 equipment sales built into guidance; Q4 margin is implied around 21%.
Cash flow was light at about $9m due to timing of customer payments, which management said have since been collected.
No 2027 guidance; management sounded upbeat but flagged ongoing cost inflation and a tougher Q4 comparison (last year had an extra week).
call.source: Midera (MFP) Q3 2026 earnings call transcript — The Motley Fool, 17 Nov 2026

watch: Whether Q4 delivers the roughly 21% margin implied by the raised guidance.
Order intake and backlog as customers plan 2027 spending.
Integration of Phoenix Innovations and further acquisitions.
